title: Official OpenClaw WebChat governed continuity

scenario.matter: A household service appointment followed over multiple fresh chat transcripts
scenario.initial_fact: The home network service appointment is Saturday at 10:00, and the technician must contact the front desk before arriving.
scenario.temporary_chatter: A lunch suggestion is temporary and must not become governed memory.
scenario.corrected_fact: The home network service appointment is Sunday at 14:00, and the technician must contact the front desk before arriving.
scenario.unrelated_session: A separate reading-list conversation with no access to the appointment matter.

hard_gates: a fresh PostgreSQL cluster migrates from schema zero to the exact supported schema before the run
Vermory, PostgreSQL, OpenClaw state, Grok state, caches, transcripts, and raw evidence remain on the external volume
the accepted run uses no privileged command and no private NewAPI gateway
OpenClaw 2026.6.11 loads the maintained Vermory plugin through the official plugin runtime
runtime inspection reports the Vermory command and the before_prompt_build and agent_end hooks
the Grok CLI backend is stateless, disables ambient memory and web search, and performs a real model call
a real Chrome page loads the official OpenClaw Control UI served by the Gateway
the browser authenticates to the Gateway and uses its WebSocket chat surface
the initial browser message is submitted through chat.send and recovered through chat.history
one completed initial agent run creates exactly one durable Vermory user observation, assistant observation, delivery, and formation schedule
model output remains an observation and no memory becomes active without explicit governance
a real formation call proposes the durable appointment fact while temporary lunch chatter remains ungoverned
the official WebChat /vermory command displays reviewable candidates without exposing authority identifiers or credentials
accepting the selected candidate through the official WebChat command creates one active governed memory
resetting the OpenClaw transcript changes its backing session id while retaining the canonical session key
a recall question in the reset transcript receives the active appointment fact through Vermory context
the reset OpenClaw transcript contains no pre-reset user or assistant message that could independently supply the recalled fact
an unrelated OpenClaw session receives none of the appointment fact before or after governance actions
correcting the appointment through the official WebChat command supersedes the old memory and creates one current replacement
a second reset transcript recalls Sunday at 14:00 and does not present Saturday at 10:00 as current
forgetting the current appointment through the official WebChat command makes the memory deleted
after a third transcript reset neither exact nor paraphrased recall can recover the deleted appointment fact
deleted and superseded appointment content is absent from current delivery, lexical projection, and vector projection
refresh reconnects the official Control UI and recovers only the active OpenClaw transcript for the selected session
restarting Vermory and the OpenClaw Gateway preserves the canonical continuity and governed lifecycle outcome
replayed browser or plugin operations do not duplicate observations, deliveries, candidates, or memories
the final browser run has no unexpected console error, credential exposure, mixed authority, or cross-session content
the public snapshot is credential-free, path-normalized, checksum-bound, and preserves every observed failed attempt separately
non_claims: the case qualifies the exact official OpenClaw and Chrome versions used, not every browser or OpenClaw release
the case treats Grok as a compatibility target and does not rank it against other models
the case does not treat OpenClaw transcripts, browser storage, or Grok private state as Vermory authority
the case does not claim automatic governance or perfect formation quality from one trajectory
the case does not qualify every OpenClaw channel, tool, or remote network topology
the case does not erase the host transcript when a governed Vermory memory is forgotten
